title: Temurah 34
description: The last daf of Temurah: the mishna ends its list of items that are burned and buried, the Gemara squares the hair of a nazirite and of a firstborn donkey with the mishna in Orla, and asks whether the ash of burned and buried items is permitted, ending with the hadran on the chapter and the tractate.
topics: 🔥 A provisional guilt offering and a doubtful bird sin offering: burned, or buried and cast into the drain?
🚫 What is buried may not be burned, and what is burned may not be buried; Rabbi Yehuda lets one be stringent
💇 Tavi before Rav Naḥman: nazirite hair buried here, burned in Orla. Impure or pure nazirite, hair or sack
🐦 A bird woven into a sack: not nullified, but why not pull it out? Rabbi Yirmeya and Rabbi Yehuda
🍞 Leavened bread is burned, as Rabbi Yehuda says; foods are burned and liquids buried
⚱️ Is the ash of buried items forbidden, and of burned consecrated items permitted?
🪵 Rami bar Ḥama: a fire that fell by itself; Rav Shemaya: the removal of the ashes, “and he shall put them”
🎉 Hadran: the end of Yesh BeKodshei Mizbe’aḥ and of Masechet Temurah

a1.he: אָשָׁם תָּלוּי — יִשָּׂרֵף, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: יִקָּבֵר. חַטַּאת הָעוֹף הַבָּאָה עַל הַסָּפֵק — תִּשָּׂרֵף, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: יְטִילֶנָּה לָאַמָּה.

a2.he: כָּל הַנִּקְבָּרִין — לֹא יִשָּׂרֵפוּ, וְכׇל הַנִּשְׂרָפִין — לֹא יִקָּבֵרוּ. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אִם רָצָה לְהַחְמִיר עַל עַצְמוֹ לִשְׂרוֹף אֶת הַנִּקְבָּרִין — רַשַּׁאי. אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אֵינוֹ מוּתָּר לְשַׁנּוֹת.

a3.he: גְּמָ׳ שְׂעַר הַנָּזִיר יִקָּבֵר. רָמֵי לֵיהּ טָבִי לְרַב נַחְמָן: תְּנַן שְׂעַר הַנָּזִיר יִקָּבֵר, וּרְמִינְהוּ: הָאוֹרֵג ״מְלֹא הַסִּיט״ מִצֶּמֶר בְּכוֹר בְּבֶגֶד — יִדָּלֵק הַבֶּגֶד, מִשְּׂעַר הַנָּזִיר וּפֶטֶר חֲמוֹר בְּשַׂק — יִדָּלֵק הַשַּׂק!

a4.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כָּאן בְּנָזִיר טָמֵא, כָּאן בְּנָזִיר טָהוֹר.

a5.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ שַׁנֵּית נָזִיר אַנָּזִיר, פֶּטֶר חֲמוֹר אַפֶּטֶר חֲמוֹר קַשְׁיָא! אִישְׁתִּיק וְלָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ וְלָא מִידֵּי. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִידֵּי שְׁמִיעַ לָךְ בְּהָא? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת — כָּאן בְּשַׂק, כָּאן בְּשֵׂעָר.

a6.he: אִיתְּמַר נָמֵי: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: כָּאן — בְּשַׂק, כָּאן — בְּשֵׂעָר. רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר: כָּאן — בְּנָזִיר טָהוֹר, כָּאן — בְּנָזִיר טָמֵא.

a7.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לִיבְטֵל שַׂק בְּרוּבָּא! אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: בְּצִיפּוּרְתָּא. צִיפּוּרְתָּא? לִישַׁלּוֹפִינְהוּ!

a8.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: הָא מַנִּי? רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא, דְּאָמַר: אִם רָצָה לְהַחְמִיר עַל עַצְמוֹ לִשְׂרוֹף אֶת הַנִּקְבָּרִים — רַשַּׁאי. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: קָא קַשְׁיָא לַן לְשַׁלּוֹפִינְהוּ, וְאַתְּ מוֹקְמַתְּ לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה!

a9.he: הָכִי קָאָמֵינָא: אִם אֶפְשָׁר לְשַׁלּוֹפִינְהוּ — מוּטָב, וְאִם לָאו — אוֹקְמַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, דְּאָמַר: אִם רָצָה לְהַחְמִיר עַל עַצְמוֹ לִשְׂרוֹף אֶת הַנִּקְבָּרִין — רַשַּׁאי.

a10.he: וְאֵלּוּ הֵן הַנִּשְׂרָפִין. אָמַר מָר: חָמֵץ בַּפֶּסַח — יִשָּׂרֵף. סְתַם לַן תַּנָּא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, דְּאָמַר: אֵין בִּיעוּר חָמֵץ אֶלָּא שְׂרֵפָה.

a11.he: תְּרוּמָה טְמֵאָה וְהָעׇרְלָה כּוּ׳. הָא כֵיצַד? אֳוכָלִין בִּשְׂרֵפָה, מַשְׁקִין בִּקְבוּרָה.

a12.he: חַטַּאת הָעוֹף כּוּ׳. תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: חַטַּאת הָעוֹף הַבָּאָה עַל הַסָּפֵק — יְטִילֶנָּה לָאַמָּה, וּמְנַתְּחָה אֵבֶר אֵבֶר, וְזוֹרְקָן לָאַמָּה, וּמִתְגַּלְגֶּלֶת וְהוֹלֶכֶת לְנַחַל קִדְרוֹן.

a13.he: כׇּל הַנִּקְבָּרִין לֹא יִשָּׂרֵפוּ כּוּ׳. מַאי טַעְמָא? מִשּׁוּם דְּנִקְבָּרִין אֶפְרָן אָסוּר, וְנִשְׂרָפִין אֶפְרָן מוּתָּר.

a14.he: וְנִקְבָּרִין אֶפְרָן אָסוּר? וְהָתַנְיָא: דַּם הַנִּדָּה וּבְשַׂר הַמֵּת שֶׁנִּפְרְכוּ — טְהוֹרִין, מַאי לַָאו טְהוֹרִין וּמוּתָּרִין? לָא, טְהוֹרִין וַאֲסוּרִין.

a15.he: מֵתִיב רַב פִּנְחָס: עוֹלַת הָעוֹף שֶׁנִּתְמַצָּה דָּמָהּ, מוּרְאָתָהּ וְנוֹצָה שֶׁלָּהּ יָצְאוּ מִידֵי מְעִילָה. מַאי לַָאו יָצְאוּ מִידֵי מְעִילָה וּמוּתָּרִין? לָא, יָצְאוּ מִידֵי מְעִילָה וַאֲסוּרִין.

a16.he: וְנִשְׂרָפִין דְּהֶקְדֵּשׁ אֶפְרָן מוּתָּר? וְהָא תַּנְיָא: כׇּל הַנִּשְׂרָפִין אֶפְרָם מוּתָּר, חוּץ מֵאֵפֶר אֲשֵׁירָה — וְאֵפֶר דְּהֶקְדֵּשׁ לְעוֹלָם אָסוּר!

a17.he: וּמִיעְרָב הוּא דְּלָא קָעָרֵיב לְהוּ וְתָנֵי לְהוּ, מִשּׁוּם דַּאֲשֵׁירָה יֵשׁ לָהּ בְּטִילָה בְּגוֹי, הֶקְדֵּשׁ אֵין לוֹ בְּטִילָה עוֹלָמִית. קָתָנֵי מִיהָא: אֵפֶר הֶקְדֵּשׁ לְעוֹלָם אָסוּר.

a18.he: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא: כְּגוֹן דְּנָפְלָה דְּלֵיקָה בַּעֲצֵי הֶקְדֵּשׁ מֵאֵלֶיהָ, כֵּיוָן דְּלָא יְדִיעַ מַאן, דְּלָא הָוֵי אִינִישׁ דְּלִמְעוֹל, דְּלִיפּוֹק אֶפְרָן לְחוּלִּין.

a19.he: רַב שְׁמַעְיָה אָמַר: כִּי תַּנְיָא הָא מַתְנִיתָא בִּתְרוּמַת הַדֶּשֶׁן תַּנְיָא, דִּלְעוֹלָם אָסוּר.

messages.text: Continued from 33b: the mishna lists the items from which benefit is forbidden that are buried and those that are burned. It has just ruled that sacrificial animals slaughtered with intent beyond their time or outside their place shall be burned. It continues:
Mishna

With regard to a provisional guilt offering brought by one who is uncertain as to whether he committed a sin that renders him liable to bring a sin offering, if he discovers that he did not sin, the offering shall be burned, as its legal status is like that of an unfit offering.

notes.he: אם שחטו וקודם זריקת דמו נודע לו שלא חטא והשתא הוו חולין שנשחטו בעזרה אבל אם לא נודע לו יאכל כשאר אשמות דאשם קרייה רחמנא בפרשת ויקרא לכפר על הספק ולהגין מן הייסורים עד שיוודע לו אם ודאי חטא ויביא חטאת כדאמרינן בכריתות בפ' בתרא (דף כו:):
notes.en: A provisional guilt offering shall be burned: if he slaughtered it, and before the sprinkling of its blood it became known to him that he had not sinned, so that now it is a non-sacred animal slaughtered in the [Temple] courtyard. But if it did not become known to him, it is eaten like other guilt offerings, for the Merciful One called it a guilt offering in the portion of Vayikra, to atone for the uncertainty and to shield him from suffering until it becomes known to him that he certainly sinned and he brings a sin offering, as we say in Keritot, in the last chapter (26b).

notes.he: כדין שאר קדשים דהא נאכל הוא לכהנים כאשם ודאי:
notes.en: A provisional guilt offering that was disqualified shall be burned, in accordance with the law of other sacrificial items, since it is eaten by the priests like a definite guilt offering.

messages.text: It shall be buried.

notes.he: משום דתני לה בברייתא בגמ' בהדי חולין שנשחטו בעזרה וכבר אמרי' במתני' לעיל דחולין שנשחטו בעזרה יקברו:
notes.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: It shall be buried: because it is taught in a baraita in the Gemara together with non-sacred animals slaughtered in the [Temple] courtyard, and we already said in the mishna above that non-sacred animals slaughtered in the courtyard shall be buried.

notes.dh: ת"ר אשם תלוי וחטאת העוף הבא על הספק
notes.he: כיון דתני להו בהדי חולין שנשחטו בעזרה קא סבר ר' יהודה יקברו ובאשם שאירע בו פיסול קתני דאי לא אירע בו פסול נאכל הוא כדתניא במס' כריתות ר' יוסי בר' יהודה אומר אשם תלוי נאכל חטאת העוף הבא על הספק אינה נאכלת מ"ט אשם תלוי אין בו אלא ספק אחת ספק קדש הוא דספק חלב אכל אכל ספק חולין דספק שומן הוא ואין בו אלא ספק חולין שנשחטו בעזרה מש"ה נאכלין ועוד משום דאמרינן מתנדב אדם ומביא אשם תלוי בכל יום שאם לא בא על חטא זה בא על [חטא] אחר:
notes.en: The Sages taught: a provisional guilt offering and a sin offering of the bird that comes due to an uncertainty. Since it teaches them together with non-sacred animals slaughtered in the [Temple] courtyard, Rabbi Yehuda holds that they shall be buried. And it speaks of a guilt offering that became disqualified, for if it did not become disqualified it is eaten, as it is taught in Tractate Keritot: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, says: A provisional guilt offering is eaten; a sin offering of the bird that comes due to an uncertainty is not eaten. What is the reason? A provisional guilt offering has only one uncertainty: perhaps it is sacred, perhaps non-sacred, for perhaps he ate forbidden fat, perhaps it was permitted fat; so it has only the uncertainty of a non-sacred animal slaughtered in the courtyard, and therefore it is eaten. And further, because we say that a person may volunteer and bring a provisional guilt offering every day, for if it does not come for this sin, it comes for another sin.

messages.text: A sin offering of the bird that comes due to an uncertainty, e.g., in the case of a woman who miscarried and she is uncertain whether it was a fetus, shall be burned, as it may not be eaten due to the uncertainty and because the nape of its neck was pinched and it was not slaughtered.

notes.he: כגון אשה שהפילה ספק ולד ספק אינו ולד כיון דחטאת [יולדת מן] העוף היא כדכתיב ובן יונה או תור לחטאת מביאתה על הספק דהואיל ואינה נקטרת לא איכפת לן אי זריק דם על הספק ואינה נאכלת דשמא לא ולד היה וחולין היא זו ונבלה היא ואין חולין נאכלין במליקה ותשרף דהוי לה כשאר קדשים פסולין ובמסכת נזיר (דף כט.) ילפינן שפיר דחטאת העוף באה על הספק:
notes.en: A sin offering of the bird, etc.: for example, a woman who miscarried, and it is uncertain whether it was a fetus or not a fetus. Since the sin offering [of a woman after childbirth] is [from] the bird, as it is written: “And a young pigeon or a turtledove for a sin offering” [Leviticus 12:6], she brings it on account of the uncertainty: since it is not burned on the altar, we are not concerned if blood is sprinkled on account of an uncertainty. And it is not eaten, for perhaps it was not a fetus, and then this bird is non-sacred and is an unslaughtered carcass, as non-sacred birds are not eaten through pinching. And it shall be burned, since it is like other disqualified sacrificial items. And in Tractate Nazir (29a) we derive properly that a sin offering of the bird comes on account of an uncertainty.

notes.he: כגון יולדת ספק זכר או נקבה או ספק הפילה נפל ספק הפילה רוח או ספק זבה מביאה קרבן ואינו נאכל:
notes.en: A sin offering of the bird that comes due to an uncertainty: for example, a woman after childbirth, uncertain whether [she bore] a male or a female, or uncertain whether she miscarried a fetus or miscarried a wind, or a woman uncertain whether she is a zava: she brings an offering, and it is not eaten.

notes.he: יש בו ב' ספיקות של איסור ספק הוא חולין בעזרה וספק איסור נבילה משום דנמלקה ואי חולין היא אי אית בה איסור נבילה מש"ה אינו נאכל:
notes.en: But a sin offering of the bird has two uncertainties of prohibition: perhaps it is a non-sacred bird in the courtyard, and perhaps it carries the prohibition of an unslaughtered carcass, since it was pinched; for if it is non-sacred, it is forbidden as a carcass. Therefore it is not eaten.

messages.text: One should cast it into the Temple courtyard drain, as the young bird will decompose and be drawn into the stream outside the Temple.

notes.he: אמת המים עוברת בעזרה ויוצאה לנחל קדרון. ואיידי דעור רך הוא מתמקמק ואינו עומד בקילוח המים:
notes.en: One should cast it into the drain: a channel of water passes through the [Temple] courtyard and goes out to the Kidron stream. And since [a young bird] is soft skin, it decomposes and does not hold together in the flow of the water.

notes.he: (כגון) [כיון] דחייבת להביא דינו כשאר קדשים פסולין דנשרפין ר' יהודה אומר יטילנה לאמה של מים היורד לנחל קדרון וזו היא קבורתו וקסבר כיון דאינו נאכל לא ישרף אלא יקבר כשאר נקברין שאין איסור [אלא] באכילה]:
notes.en: Shall be burned: since she is obligated to bring it, its law is like that of other disqualified sacrificial items, which are burned. Rabbi Yehuda says: One should cast it into the water channel that runs down to the Kidron stream, and this is its burial. He holds that since it is not eaten, it is not burned but buried, like other items that are buried, whose prohibition is only in eating.

messages.text: The principle is: All items that are buried shall not be burned, and all items that are burned shall not be buried.

notes.he: דלמא אתי איניש ואשכח להו ואכיל להו:
notes.en: All items that are burned shall not be buried: lest a person come and find them and eat them.

notes.he: בגמ' מפרש טעמא:
notes.en: And items that are buried shall not be burned: the Gemara explains the reason.

messages.text: If one wished to impose a stringency upon himself by burning items that are to be buried, he is permitted to burn them.

@Rabbi Yehuda One is not permitted to change the method of destruction, as this could lead to a leniency, since it is permitted to derive benefit from the ashes of items that require burning, whereas it is not permitted to derive benefit from the ashes of items that require burial.
Gemara
Among the items from which benefit is prohibited, the mishna states that the hair of a nazirite shall be buried.
We learned in the mishna that the hair of a nazirite shall be buried; but one can raise a contradiction from another mishna (Orla 3:3):
messages.lead: With regard to this halakha, Tavi raised a contradiction before Rav Naḥman:

messages.text: One who weaves one sit, the distance between one’s index and middle fingers, of the wool of a firstborn animal, from which deriving benefit is prohibited in accordance with the halakha of all sacrificial animals, in a garment, the garment shall be ignited. Similarly, if one weaves from the hair of a nazirite, or from the hair of a firstborn donkey, in a sack, the sack shall be ignited.

notes.he: מלא הרחקת גודל מאצבע מה שהוא יכול להרחיק:
notes.en: Gemara. A full sit: the full spread of the thumb from the finger, as far as one can spread them. [Rashi measures from the thumb; the Davidson English gives the distance between the index and middle fingers.]

notes.he: אסור בהנאה דקדשים הוא:
notes.en: Wool of a firstborn: benefit from it is forbidden, for it is a sacrificial item.

notes.he: גבי צמר נקט בגד וגבי שער נקט שק כי אורחא דמילתא:
notes.en: Shall be ignited: with wool it speaks of a garment and with hair it speaks of a sack, as is the usual way of things.

messages.text: There is no contradiction. Here, the ruling of the mishna that teaches that the hair of a nazirite is buried, is stated with regard to a nazirite who became ritually impure, and who must therefore shave his head and begin a new naziriteship.
messages.quote: the hair of a nazirite shall be buried

notes.he: שער נזיר טהור ישרף דשרפה כתיבא ביה דכתיב ונתן על האש וגו'. שער נזיר טמא לא כתיב ביה שרפה:
notes.en: The hair of a ritually pure nazirite shall be burned, for burning is written with regard to it, as it is written: “And put it on the fire,” etc. [Numbers 6:18]. With regard to the hair of a ritually impure nazirite, burning is not written.

messages.text: And there, the ruling of the mishna that states that the hair is burned, is stated with regard to the hair of a ritually pure nazirite, who shaves his head upon successful completion of his naziriteship. At this stage his hair is burned, in accordance with the verses: “And this is the law of the nazirite, when the days of his consecration are fulfilled…And the nazirite shall shave his consecrated head at the door of the Tent of Meeting, and shall take the hair of his consecrated head and put it on the fire that is under the sacrifice of peace offerings” (Numbers 6:13–18).

verse.he: וְגִלַּח הַנָּזִיר פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד אֶת־רֹאשׁ נִזְרוֹ וְלָקַח אֶת־שְׂעַר רֹאשׁ נִזְרוֹ וְנָתַן עַל־הָאֵשׁ אֲשֶׁר־תַּחַת זֶבַח הַשְּׁלָמִים׃
verse.en: The nazirite shall then shave their consecrated hair, at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, and take those locks of consecrated hair and put them on the fire that is under the sacrifice of well-being.

messages.text: You have answered the contradiction with regard to a nazirite and a nazirite. But the contradiction with regard to a firstborn donkey and a firstborn donkey still poses a difficulty, as the mishna here states that the animal and its hair are buried, whereas the mishna in tractate Orla teaches that its hair is burned.
messages.quote: with regard to a nazirite who became ritually impure

messages.text: Rav Naḥman was silent and said nothing to Tavi about the contradiction.
Have you heard anything with regard to this from others?

Here, where the mishna states that the hair of a firstborn donkey is burned, it is referring to a case where the hair was weaved in a sack, whereas there, where the mishna rules that the hair is buried, it is referring to the hair by itself.
messages.lead: Tavi said to him: This is what Rav Sheshet said in response to the contradiction:

notes.he: הא דקתני ידלק היינו שארג שער נזיר ופטר חמור בשק דאי אמרת יקבר אתי איניש ומתהני בה הואיל ואינו כלה עד לאחר זמן ומתני' בשער עצמו שלא נארג ואידי ואידי בטהור או טמא:
notes.en: Here, in a sack: that which it teaches, “shall be ignited,” is where one wove hair of a nazirite and of a firstborn donkey into a sack, for if you were to say it is buried, a person would come and derive benefit from it, since it does not decay until after a long time. And our mishna is about the hair itself, which was not woven. And both this and that are about a pure or an impure [nazirite].

messages.text: These responses of Rav Naḥman and Rav Sheshet were also stated by other Sages.

Here, in tractate Orla, the mishna is referring to a case where the hair of the nazirite or firstborn donkey was weaved in a sack, whereas there it is referring to the hair of the nazirite or firstborn donkey itself.
And here, in tractate Orla, the mishna is referring to a ritually pure nazirite, and there the mishna is referring to the hair of a ritually impure nazirite.

notes.he: ואידי ואידי בשק. ופטר חמור לקמן משני לה ומוקים לה כר' יהודה:
notes.en: And Rabbi Elazar says, etc.: and both this and that are about a sack. And as for the firstborn donkey, the Gemara resolves it below and establishes it in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda.

messages.text: Even if there is a difference between the hair itself and hair weaved in a sack, let the hair that was weaved in a sack be nullified by the majority, i.e., the other materials weaved into the sack, and therefore the sack need not be burned.
messages.quote: the hair was weaved in a sack

notes.he: דהא קתני שער נזיר ופטר חמור בשק במשמע מעט ממנו בבגד גדול של היתר. ואי קשיא הא דאמרי' במס' נדה (דף סא:) בגד שאבד בו כלאים ה"ז לא ימכרנו לעובד כוכבי' ואמאי אסור למוכרו וליבטל ההוא חוט ברובא כי היכי דאמרי' הכא הא לאו פירכא היא דבכלאים לא אמר ליבטל ברובא דעיקר איסור כלאים לא אסרה תורה אלא על ידי תערובת וכלאים מתרגמינן עירובין ולא שייך בהו ביטול:
notes.en: Let it be nullified by the majority: for it teaches “the hair of a nazirite and a firstborn donkey in a sack,” implying a little of it in a large garment of permitted material. And if you ask about what we say in Tractate Nidda (61b), that a garment in which a thread of diverse kinds was lost may not be sold to a gentile: why is it forbidden to sell it? Let that thread be nullified by the majority, just as we say here! That is no refutation, for with regard to diverse kinds one does not say “let it be nullified by the majority,” since the Torah forbade diverse kinds essentially only through a mixture, and we translate kilayim [in Aramaic] as “mixtures,” so nullification does not apply to them.

notes.he: א"ל רב טבי ובשק אמאי ידלק השק וניבטל האי שער בשק ברובה:
notes.en: Rav Tavi said to him: And with a sack, why should the sack be ignited? Let this hair be nullified by the majority in the sack. [Rabbeinu Gershom puts this challenge in the mouth of Tavi, whom he calls Rav Tavi; the Davidson English gives it to Rav Naḥman.]

messages.text: That mishna is dealing with a case where one used the prohibited hair to weave an ornamental design of a bird into the sack. Such a design is considered significant in its own right, and consequently it is not nullified by the majority.
messages.quote: let the hair that was weaved in a sack be nullified by the majority

notes.he: שעשה מן האיסור צורת צפור בשק דחשיב דמיפה ליה לכולי שק ולא מיבטל:
notes.en: With a bird: that he made from the forbidden material the shape of a bird in the sack, which is significant, as it beautifies the whole sack, and it is not nullified.

notes.he: א"ר פפא בציפורתא כגון שארג מאותו שער נזיר בשק דמות עוף דמלאכה חשובה היא הלכך לא בטיל וידלק:
notes.en: Rav Pappa said: With a bird: for example, one wove from that nazirite hair, in the sack, the image of a bird, which is significant work; therefore it is not nullified, and it shall be ignited.

messages.text: Why should the entire sack be burned on account of the bird design? Let him remove any designs weaved into the sack with the prohibited hair, and the remaining materials should be permitted.
messages.quote: an ornamental design of a bird

notes.he: ואכתי אמאי ידלק ונשלפינהו שלופי לאותו השער מן השק ויקברנו ולא ישרף השק:
notes.en: And still, why should it be ignited? Let him pull that hair out of the sack and bury it, and the sack need not be burned.

messages.text: In accordance with whose opinion is this mishna in tractate Orla? It is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda, who said that if one wished to impose a stringency upon himself by burning items that are to be buried, he is permitted to do so.
messages.quote: If one wished to impose a stringency upon himself

notes.he: דהשתא ס"ד דהכי מתרץ הא מני דאזיל לחומרא ר' יהודה היא:
notes.en: In accordance with whom is this: for now it enters our mind that he resolves it this way: in accordance with whom is this ruling, which goes toward stringency? It is Rabbi Yehuda.

notes.dh: הא מני דישרף ר' יהודה היא דאמר במתני' אם רצה להחמיר כו'
notes.he: א"ל קשיא לן לשלופינהו דאנא קא בעינא למעבד ליה תקנתא דלא ישרף כלל ומוקמת לה את כר' יהודה דישרף:
notes.en: In accordance with whom is this, that it shall be burned? It is Rabbi Yehuda, who said in our mishna: “If he wished to impose a stringency,” etc. He said to him: It is difficult for us, “let him remove them,” for I am seeking to give it a remedy so that it is not burned at all, and you establish it in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, that it shall be burned!

messages.text: We raised a difficulty that one should remove the bird designs, and you establish that the mishna is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda? Even according to Rabbi Yehuda, in a case where one can remove the prohibited portion of the sack and use the rest of it, why would he burn it, even as a stringency?
messages.quote: It is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda

notes.he: דאפשר בתקנה ואת מוקמת כר' יהודה היכא דאיכא תקנתא מי אמר רבי יהודה אמר ליה הכי קאמינא לה א"א לשלופינהו מוטב ודקא קשיא לך פטר חמור אפטר חמור הא דקתני ישרף ובמתני' יקבר לא תישני בנזיר (כאן בטמא כאן בטהור) אלא אוקמה כר' יהודה כולה ומיתוקמא שפיר:
notes.en: He said to him: It is difficult for us, “let him remove them”: for a remedy is possible, and you establish it in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda? Where there is a remedy, did Rabbi Yehuda say [one may burn]? He said to him: This is what I am saying: if it is possible to remove them, fine. And as for what posed a difficulty for you, firstborn donkey against firstborn donkey, that here it teaches “shall be burned” and in our mishna “shall be buried”: do not resolve it with the nazirite (here an impure one, there a pure one); rather, establish all of it in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, and it is properly resolved.

messages.text: This is what I meant to say: If it is possible to remove it from the sack, fine;

notes.he: (כלל) לא קאי כלל אקושיא דליבטלינהו ברובא אלא אקושיא קמייתא דהתם קתני ידלק ובמתני' יקבר והלשון לאו דוקא:
notes.en: If it is possible to remove them, fine: this does not refer at all to the difficulty “let them be nullified by the majority,” but to the first difficulty, that there it teaches “shall be ignited” and in our mishna “shall be buried”; and the wording is not exact.

notes.he: א"ל הכי קאמינא אם אפשר לשלופינהו [מוטב] (מותר) דלא ישרף ואם אי אפשר לשלופינהו [ידלק] אוקמא להא מתני' דקתני ידלק כר' יהודה דאמר אם רצה להחמיר כו':
notes.en: He said to him: This is what I am saying: if it is possible to remove them, fine, so that it is not burned; and if it is not possible to remove them, [it shall be ignited]: establish this mishna, which teaches “shall be ignited,” in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, who said: “If he wished to impose a stringency,” etc.

messages.text: and if not, there is a third answer to the contradiction that Tavi raised before Rav Naḥman: Interpret the mishna in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda, who said that if one wished to impose a stringency upon himself by burning items that are to be buried, he is permitted to do so.

notes.he: אימר דאמר ר' יהודה אם רצה להחמיר היינו כשהן בפ"ע הנקבר ע"י תערובת כגון שק זה מי שמעת ליה דישרף תנא אם לא רצה לחלוץ ולקבור אלא לשרוף יחד רשאי כר' יהודה:
notes.en: One may say: when Rabbi Yehuda said “if he wished to impose a stringency,” that is when the items are by themselves; but a buried item in a mixture, such as this sack, did you hear him say that it is burned? [The answer:] the tanna teaches that if he did not wish to pull it out and bury it, but rather to burn it all together, he may, in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda.

messages.caption: Tavi’s contradiction: our mishna buries the hair of a nazirite and a firstborn donkey, the mishna in Orla burns a sack woven from it, and the answers given.

messages.text: And these are the items that are burned: Leavened bread.

The Master said in the mishna that leavened bread on Passover shall be burned. If so, the tanna taught us an unattributed mishna in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda, who said that the eradication of leavened bread can be performed only by means of burning. By contrast, the Rabbis rule that leavened bread may be eradicated through any manner of destruction.

The mishna further teaches that ritually impure teruma shall be burned. And with regard to orla and diverse kinds of food crops sown in a vineyard, those items whose appropriate manner of destruction is to be burned shall be burned, and those items whose appropriate manner of destruction is to be buried shall be buried.

notes.he: מדליקין את הנר ואת השמן ואת הפת האפוי (את התנור) כלומר דנהנה ממנה כהן בתרומה טמאה להסקה וניחוש אי משהי לה לתרומה לצורך הסקה דדלמא אתי בה לידי תקלה שמא יאכלנה:
notes.en: One may light the lamp with the oil and the baked bread (the oven): that is, the priest derives benefit from impure teruma for kindling. And should we not be concerned that if he keeps the teruma for kindling, it may lead him to a stumbling block, lest he eat it? [This refers to the clause of the mishna on 33b permitting one to ignite a fire with bread and oil of impure teruma.]

notes.he: פת זריק לה לבין (עינים) [העצים] ומינכר מילתא דלא חזי (היסק) [תו לאכילה ושמן בכלי מאוס:
notes.en: Bread: he throws it among the wood, and it is evident that it is no longer fit for eating; and oil, in a repulsive vessel. [Reading with the bracketed corrections in the printed text.]

messages.text: How so, i.e., what is an item whose appropriate manner of destruction is to be burned? Foods are items whose appropriate manner of destruction is by burning; and liquids are items whose appropriate manner of destruction is by burial.

notes.he: כגון אוכלין ישרף ואת שדרכו ליקבר כגון משקין דלא אפשר להו בשריפה יקבר:
notes.en: That whose way is to be burned, such as foods, shall be burned; and that whose way is to be buried, such as liquids, which cannot be burned, shall be buried.

messages.text: A sin offering of the bird that comes due to an uncertainty shall be burned; Rabbi Yehuda says that one should cast it into the Temple courtyard drain. With regard to the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda, it is taught in a baraita:
messages.quote: A sin offering of the bird that comes due to an uncertainty

messages.text: With regard to a sin offering of the bird that comes due to an uncertainty, one should cast it into the Temple courtyard drain. And how is this performed? He severs the animal limb by limb and then tosses all the limbs into the drain, and each limb rolls out continuously with the liquids in the drain to the Kidron River outside Jerusalem.
§ The mishna teaches that all items that are buried shall not be burned, and all items that are burned shall not be buried. What is the reason that items that are buried may not be burned?
messages.quote: All items that are buried shall not be burned

notes.he: נקברין לא ישרפו משום דנקברים אפרן אסור ואתו למישרייא:
notes.en: What is the reason that items that are buried shall not be burned? Because the ash of items that are buried is forbidden, and people would come to permit it.

messages.text: This is because with regard to items that are buried, their ashes are prohibited, but with regard to items that are burned, their ashes are permitted. Accordingly, due to a concern that one who burns an item that should be buried might derive benefit from the ashes, the Sages prohibited the burning of any item that is buried.

notes.he: (הקדש קשיא) וניחא אי גרסי' נשרפין אפרן מותר וכן גרסי' במקצת ספרים מיהו יש ליישב דלאלימותא נקטוה אפר הקדש הכא דמתני' דנשחטין חוץ לזמנן דאפרן מותר ומשום דבסמוך מותיב מינייהו דקאמר ונשרפין דהקדש דאפרן מותר והתנא נסיב ליה הכא:
notes.en: And items that are burned are permitted: (consecrated property is difficult). It is fine if we read “items that are burned, their ash is permitted” [without mention of consecrated property], and so we read in some books. However, it can be reconciled: they took the ash of consecrated property here to strengthen the point, [namely the ash] of our mishna’s [sacrificial animals] slaughtered beyond their time, whose ash is permitted; and because just below the Gemara raises an objection from them, saying “And items of consecrated property that are burned, is their ash permitted?”, the tanna took it up here.

notes.he: אותן שדינן ליקבר אם שרפן אפרן אסור הלכך אסור לשנות שאם היה שורפן היו נהנין מאפרן כדקי"ל דנשרפין אפרן מותר:
notes.en: Items that are buried: those whose law is to be buried, if one burned them, their ash is forbidden. Therefore it is forbidden to change, for if he were to burn them, people would derive benefit from their ash, as we hold that the ash of items that are burned is permitted.

messages.text: And is the halakha with regard to items that are buried that their ashes are prohibited? But isn’t it taught in a baraita:

With regard to the blood of a menstruating woman and the flesh of a corpse, which normally render one ritually impure whether they are dry or wet, in a case where they dried up and crumbled, they are ritually pure.

notes.he: אע"ג דקי"ל במס' נדה (דף נד:) מטמאין לחין ויבשין היכא דנעשו אפר בעלמא טהורין אם אין שם מלא תרווד רקב ומותר בהנאה ובשר המת מן הנקברין הוא ושרי אפרו:
notes.en: The blood of a menstruating woman and the flesh of a corpse: even though we hold, in Tractate Nidda (54b), that they render impure whether moist or dry, where they have become mere ash they are pure, if there is not a full ladle of corpse dust there; and [the questioner takes it that] benefit from them is permitted. And the flesh of a corpse is among the items that are buried, yet its ash is permitted.

messages.text: What, is it not correct to infer from the baraita that they are ritually pure and one is permitted to derive benefit from them, despite the fact that a corpse is an item that is buried?

notes.he: שדרכן ליקבר אם לא נקברו וכבר הופרכו מעצמן ונעשו אפר (טהורין) מותרין [מאי לאו טהורים ומותרים] אפרן בהנאה:
notes.en: The blood of a menstruating woman and the flesh of a corpse, whose way is to be buried: if they were not buried and had already crumbled by themselves and become ash, they are permitted. [What, is it not that they are pure and] their ash is permitted for benefit?

messages.text: No, the baraita means that they are pure only in the sense that they do not render one ritually impure, but it is nevertheless prohibited to derive benefit from them.

With regard to a burnt offering of the bird whose blood was squeezed onto the wall of the altar in the appropriate manner, its crop and its feathers, which do not ascend upon the altar, have been removed from the halakhot of misuse.
messages.lead: Rav Pineḥas raises an objection from another baraita:

notes.he: שנעשית מצותה:
notes.en: Whose blood was squeezed: whose mitzva has been performed.

notes.he: נקברין נינהו דאמרי' בפ"ק דיומא (דף כא.) מוראה ונוצה ודישון מזבח הפנימי והמנורה נבלעין במקומן:
notes.en: Its crop and its feathers: they are among the items that are buried, as we say in the first chapter of Yoma (21a): the crop and the feathers, and the ashes removed from the inner altar and from the Candelabrum, are swallowed up in their place.

messages.text: What, is it not correct to infer from this that they have been removed entirely from the halakhot of misuse and are no longer consecrated? And therefore one is permitted to derive benefit from them, despite the fact that the crop and feathers are buried, as they are tossed to the eastern side of the altar and are swallowed in their place. Evidently, it is permitted to derive benefit from items that are buried.

notes.he: אפילו לכתחלה אם חפר ונטלן:
notes.en: And are permitted: even initially, if one dug and took them.

notes.he: דמה על קיר המזבח מוראה ונוצה שלה שאינה בהקטרה יצאו מידי מעילה שכבר יש להן שעת היתר שאין בהן מצות הקטרה וכבר נעשית מצותן דאין בהן שום מצוה הלכך יצאו מידי מעילה אבל היא עצמה (כשרה) [בשרה] מועלין בה עד שתצא לבית הדשן דלא נעשת מצותה עד (שהוסק) [שהוקטרה] שאין בה שעת היתר לכהנים דכולה כליל והא מוראה ונוצה דנקברין הן כדתנן המוראה והנוצה נבלעין בארץ במקומן ע"י נס וקתני יצאו מידי מעילה מאי לאו יצאו מידי מעילה ומותר:
notes.en: A burnt offering of the bird whose blood was squeezed onto the wall of the altar: its crop and its feathers, which are not burned on the altar, have gone out from misuse, for they already have a time of permission: they have no mitzva of burning on the altar, and their mitzva has already been performed, as no mitzva remains in them; therefore they have gone out from misuse. But one is liable for misuse of its flesh itself until it goes out to the place of the ashes, since its mitzva is not performed until it is burned, and it has no time of permission for the priests, as it is entirely burned. And these, the crop and the feathers, are among the items that are buried, as we learned: the crop and the feathers are swallowed into the ground in their place by a miracle. And it teaches that they have gone out from misuse: what, is it not that they have gone out from misuse and are permitted?

messages.text: No, the baraita means that they have been removed from the halakhot of misuse, but one is nevertheless prohibited to derive benefit from them.
messages.quote: they have been removed entirely from the halakhot of misuse

messages.text: And is it the halakha with regard to consecrated items that are burned that their ashes are permitted? But isn’t it taught in a baraita:

With regard to all prohibited items that must be burned, their ashes are permitted, except for wood from a tree used as part of idolatrous rites [ashera]. And ash of consecrated property is prohibited forever.

notes.he: כגון חמץ ותרומה וערלה וכלאי הכרם אפרן מותר לכיבוס בגדים:
notes.en: All items that are burned: such as leavened bread, teruma, orla and diverse kinds of the vineyard; their ash is permitted for laundering clothes.

messages.text: And the tanna did not combine them into one phrase and teach them together, because an ashera can become permitted, as it has the option of nullification by a gentile, whereas consecrated property never has the option of nullification.
messages.lead: Before summarizing the question, the Gemara explains why the baraita teaches the halakhot with regard to an ashera and consecrated property separately:

notes.dh: לעולם אסור ומיערב לא עריב כו'
notes.he: האי מקשה מפרש ואזיל לברייתא דלא תיקשי ליה היא גופה כיון דאפר עצי אשרה ואפר הקדש שניהן אסורין אמאי פליג להו מהדדי ולא תני חוץ מעצי אשרה ואפר הקדש ולא ליתני לעולם אסור ומפרש משום דאינן שוין דאשירה יש לה ביטול ביד עובד כוכבים כדקיי"ל במס' ע"ז מנין לעובד כוכבים שפוסל אלוהו דכתיב פסילי אלהיהם וכתיב ולקחת לך בפ' ר' ישמעאל (ע"ז דף נב.) בגמ' עבודת כוכבים של עובד כוכבים אסור כו':
notes.en: Is prohibited forever; and he did not combine, etc.: the one raising this difficulty goes on to explain the baraita, so that it should not itself pose a difficulty for him: since the ash of ashera wood and the ash of consecrated property are both forbidden, why does it separate them from each other, and not teach “except for ashera wood and ash of consecrated property” without teaching “is prohibited forever”? And he explains: because they are not alike, for an ashera can be nullified by a gentile, as we hold in Tractate Avoda Zara: from where is it derived that a gentile can disqualify his god? For it is written “the carved images of their gods” and it is written “and take it for yourself” [Deuteronomy 7:25], in the chapter Rabbi Yishmael (Avoda Zara 52a), in the Gemara on “An idol belonging to a gentile is forbidden,” etc.

notes.he: והאי [דלא] קא עריב להו דלא אמר חוץ מעצי אשירה ואפר הקדש אלא קא הדר ואמר ואפר הקדש לעולם אסור משום דאשירה יש לה בטילה בעובד כוכבים דאי בטיל לה עובד כוכבים מותרת:
notes.en: No: they have gone out [from misuse] and are forbidden. And the reason he does not combine them, saying “except for ashera wood and ash of consecrated property,” but goes back and says “and ash of consecrated property is prohibited forever,” is because an ashera can be nullified by a gentile: if a gentile nullifies it, it is permitted.

messages.text: In any event, the baraita teaches that the ash of consecrated property is prohibited forever.
messages.quote: ash of consecrated property is prohibited forever

messages.text: In general, it is permitted to derive benefit from the ash of burnt consecrated property. But this is the halakha either in a case where the consecrated property has been disqualified in some manner, as in the mishna, when its sanctity is weakened, or in a case where one would be liable for misuse of consecrated property when burning it. In such a situation, it is the misuse which causes the consecrated property to become non-sacred.
messages.quote: the ash of consecrated property is prohibited forever

messages.text: By contrast, the baraita is dealing with a case where the ash remains prohibited, for example, if a fire fell by itself onto consecrated wood. Since it cannot be known who burned the wood, as there is no person who misused the wood in order that its ash should change to non-sacred status, the ash is therefore prohibited.

notes.he: דאי הדליקה אדם מעל המסיק ונפק אפר לחולין והנך דטעונין שרפה בלא שום מעילה יצא אפרן לחולין דקלישא קדושתייהו הואיל ונפסלו והא דקתני אפר הקדש אסור היכא דליכא מעילה ולא הוה איניש דלמעול ובעצי הקדש קאמר:
notes.en: This is the reading: “there is no person who misused.” For if a person had kindled it, the one who lit it would have misused it, and the ash would go out to non-sacred status. And as for those items that require burning, even without any misuse their ash goes out to non-sacred status, since their sanctity is weakened, as they have been disqualified. And that which it teaches, “ash of consecrated property is forbidden,” is where there is no misuse and there is no person who misused, and it speaks of consecrated wood.

notes.dh: הכא במאי עסקינן דאפר הקדש לעולם אסור
notes.he: כגון שנפלה דליקה מאליה בהקדש דלא הוה איניש דלמעול בה דליק' מפיק אפר לחולין דזהו דין מעילה אם הוא דבר שמצותה בשריפה מאחר ששרפו שנעשה מצותו אין בו מעילה ואפרו מותר ואם הוא דבר שאין מצותו בשרפה כיון ששרפו שמעל בו יצא לחולין ואפרו מותר אבל כשנפלה דליקה מאליה דלא מעל בה אדם דלא יצאת לחולין הלכך אותו אפר הקדש לעולם אסור. והיינו טעמא דהמועל (אמר) חייב קרבן מעילה משום דכיון דמעל בה הוציאה לחולין ומשום [הכי] (כן) מביא קרבן מעילה דהוציא הקדש לחולין:
notes.en: With what are we dealing here, that ash of consecrated property is prohibited forever? For example, where a fire fell by itself onto consecrated property, so there was no person who misused it whose misuse would take the ash out to non-sacred status. For this is the law of misuse: if it is an item whose mitzva is burning, once he burned it, its mitzva has been performed, there is no misuse in it, and its ash is permitted. And if it is an item whose mitzva is not burning, once he burned it, since he misused it, it went out to non-sacred status and its ash is permitted. But when a fire fell by itself, since no person misused it, it did not go out to non-sacred status; therefore that ash of consecrated property is prohibited forever. And this is the reason that one who misuses is liable to bring an offering for misuse: since he misused it, he took it out to non-sacred status, and for that reason he brings an offering for misuse, for he took consecrated property out to non-sacred status.

messages.text: When this baraita was taught, it was taught with regard to the removal of the ashes every morning, i.e., the rite in which the priest removes some of the ashes from upon the altar and places them on the ground beside the altar. In this instance, the halakha is that the ash is prohibited forever.
messages.quote: the ash of consecrated property is prohibited forever

notes.he: דאפר הקדש אסור במלא קומץ של הדשן קאמר שהכהן תורם בכל יום שחרית ונותנו אצל המזבח כדאמר בפ"ב דיומא (דף כד.) נאמר כאן והרים ונאמר להלן והרים מה להלן בקומצו אף כאן בקומצו:
notes.en: When this was taught: that the ash of consecrated property is forbidden, it speaks of the full handful of the ashes that the priest removes every day in the morning and places beside the altar, as it says in the second chapter of Yoma (24a): it is stated here “and he shall take up” and it is stated there “and he shall take up”; just as there it is with his handful, so too here it is with his handful.

notes.dh: רב שמעיה אמר כי תניא ההיא
notes.he: דאפר הקדש לעולם אסור בתרומת הדשן ל"א היינו אפר הטעון גניזה:
notes.en: Rav Shemaya said: When that was taught, that ash of consecrated property is prohibited forever, it was with regard to the removal of the ashes. Another version: that is, ash that requires storing away.

messages.text: The verse states: “And he shall take up the ashes to which the fire has consumed the burnt offering on the altar, and he shall put them beside the altar” (Leviticus 6:3). The term “and he shall put them” indicates that he shall place them down gently, rather than cast them down. Additionally, the emphasis on “them” in the term “and he shall put them” teaches that he shall put all of them. Finally, it is derived from the superfluous “and” in the term “and he shall put them” that he shall not scatter the ashes.
messages.lead: As it is taught in a baraita with regard to the removal of the ashes:

verse.he: וְלָבַשׁ הַכֹּהֵן מִדּוֹ בַד וּמִכְנְסֵי־בַד יִלְבַּשׁ עַל־בְּשָׂרוֹ וְהֵרִים אֶת־הַדֶּשֶׁן אֲשֶׁר תֹּאכַל הָאֵשׁ אֶת־הָעֹלָה עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּחַ וְשָׂמוֹ אֵצֶל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ׃
verse.en: The priest shall dress in linen raiment, with linen breeches next to his body; and he shall take up the ashes to which the fire has reduced the burnt offering on the altar and place them beside the altar.

messages.text: The ruling of the baraita that all of the ashes must be placed in the ground indicates that even after the consecrated item is burned, the ashes remain sanctified and are prohibited.

notes.he: וכיון דטעון גניזה אסור בהנאה:
notes.en: “And he shall put them” beside the altar; “and he shall put them,” all of it: and since it requires storing away, benefit from it is forbidden.

notes.he: כדתניא ושמו אצל המזבח יכול למימר ושם אצל המזבח אלא חד ושמו מיבעי ליה ושמו כולו ואידך ושמו דנפיק מוי"ו מיבעי ליה לושמו בנחת שלא יפזר סליק:
notes.en: As it is taught: “And he shall put them beside the altar.” It could have said “and he shall put” beside the altar; rather, one “and he shall put them” is needed for “he shall put all of it,” and the other “and he shall put them,” which comes from the vav, is needed for “he shall put them gently,” so that he does not scatter them. Concluded.
